title: Four equivalent characterizations of universally injective morphisms, including surjectivity of the diagonal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma assembles the four standard characterizations of a universally injective (equivalently radicial) morphism: injectivity of the induced maps on field-valued points, universal injectivity, radicality, and surjectivity of the diagonal (statement lines 1794-1810). The counted proof is a chain of four implications plus the diagonal equivalence, and it is not a citation: it uses the section/point dictionary for base changes to the spectrum of a field, the choice of a common field containing two residue fields to detect non-injectivity, the criterion for purely inseparable extensions by uniqueness of embeddings, and finally the description of points of the fibre product by quadruples involving a prime ideal in a tensor product of residue fields (proof lines 1812-1884). It is H2: the proof is long and has to keep four conditions in play, but every step is carried out in the counted span and the inputs are standard, so no independent research-level claim is made.
